results.name: Parcel_Boundaries_of_Indiana_Current
results.title: Parcel Boundaries of Indiana Current
results.description: This data layer is an Esri file geodatabase polygon feature class that contains parcel boundaries maintained by county agencies in Indiana. It was released by the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO) on February 1, 2022. The IGIO compiled the data as part of the Indiana Data Harvest program between the Indiana Geographic Information Council (IGIC) and all Indiana counties to provide the most accurate framework data for the citizens of Indiana. These layers include address points, street centerlines, land parcels, and governmental boundaries.
results.snippet:
This dataset was developed to provide accurate parcel boundaries for Indiana, as part of Indiana's annual GIS Data harvest Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI) of the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO).

If attempting to download this data in shapefile or file geodatabase format on indianamap.org, please note that this dataset is too large to fit in a shapefile and generating a geodatabase does not perform well in the ArcGIS Hub interface. To download a pre-zipped file geodatabase, please go to https://countydataharvest.in.gov/statewide/2022/DataHarvest_2022_SingleFGDB_20230125.zip.
results.accessInformation: This data set was created as part of the Indiana Geographic Information Office's GIS Data Harvest Program. The source data used to create this dataset was provided by Indiana counties.
results.licenseInfo: CREDIT - It is requested, but not required, that the Indiana GIS Data Harvest Program be cited in any products generated from this data set. If citing, the following source citation language should be included: [Parcel Boundaries of Indiana 2021: Parcel Boundaries Maintained by County Agencies in Indiana, (Indiana Geographic Information Office, File Geodatabase, Polygon Feature Class), 20220201].

results.name: Public_School
results.title: Public School
results.description:
This dataset is designed to represent and identify the boundaries of public school facilities within Lexington-Fayette County. The dataset is created by leveraging the appropriate boundaries in the GIS parcel dataset. The location of the public school facilities is updated through public record and coordination with the Fayette County Public School. The location for the certified private schools is updated through public record for certified private schools from the Kentucky Department of Education. The public school facilities are continuously updated. This dataset participates in a topology with the parcel dataset to assure coincident geometry during parcel editing.

As part of the basemap data layers, the school boundary map layer is an integral part of the Lexington Fayette-Urban County Government Geographic Information System. Basemap data layers are accessed by personnel in most LFUCG divisions for basic applications such as viewing, querying, and map output production. More advanced user applications may focus on thematic mapping, summarization of data by geography, or planning purposes (including defining boundaries, managing assets and facilities, integrating attribute databases with geographic features, spatial analysis, and presentation output).
results.snippet: Boundaries of public school facilities within Lexington-Fayette County, Kentucky.

results.name: Public_School_Point
results.title: Public School Point
results.description:
This dataset is designed to represent and identify the general locations of public school facilities within Lexington-Fayette County. The dataset is programmatically created and updated by converting the polygon centroids of the LFUCG School boundary polygon layer to a point layer. The location of the public school facilities is updated through public record and coordination with the Fayette County Public School. The location for the certified private schools is updated through public record for certified private schools from the Kentucky Department of Education. The public school facilities are continuously updated. This dataset participates in a topology with the parcel dataset to assure coincident geometry during parcel editing.


The data is in ESRI feature class format, but can be exported to any number of supported formats, including shapefile and dxf. The native projection for the data is Kentucky State Plane North (NAD83), but may have been reprojected for use in other applications. Please check metadata to determine current projection.

results.title: Keystone Opportunity Zones Imagery_WFL1
results.description:
Purpose: This map layer includes information, data, and shapefiles regarding tax credit programs for properties in Fayette County, PA. The major features showcased in this layer are Keystone Opportunity Zones. There are also transportation routes, municipality boundaries, and countywide parcels. This visual also includes 2026 shapefiles on PA counties and generalized US state boundaries. There are zoom levels set for all labels and symbology in the feature class layers. Additionally, this layer uses a the Mercator projection system, which is used for all online WebGIS maps/layers.

 

Additional Info:

Keystone Opportunity Zone (KOZ)

Purpose:
A statewide economic development program that reduces or eliminates many state and local taxes for businesses, property owners, and residents located in designated underdeveloped or underutilized areas.

Key Features:

  • Designated geographic zones where tax burden can be significantly reduced or reduced to zero for qualified businesses and residents.
  • Tax exemptions/abatements can apply to corporate net income tax, personal income tax, sales/use tax, and many local taxes.
  • Typically used to spur investment, development, and job creation in areas needing revitalization.

Who it’s for:
Businesses (including firms relocating within PA under certain conditions) and property owners within the KOZ.

results.title: Keystone Enterprise Zones Imagery_WFL1
results.description:
Purpose: This map layer includes information, data, and shapefiles regarding tax credit programs for properties in Fayette County, PA. The major features showcased in this layer are Keystone Enterprise Zones. There are also transportation routes, municipality boundaries, and countywide parcels. This visual also includes 2026 shapefiles on PA counties and generalized US state boundaries. There are zoom levels set for all labels and symbology in the feature class layers. Additionally, this layer uses a the Mercator projection system, which is used for all online WebGIS maps/layers.

 

Additional Info:

Keystone Enterprise Zone (KEZ) / Enterprise Zone Programs

Context in Pennsylvania Programs:

  • Under the Keystone Communities Program, communities can receive designations that include things like Keystone Enterprise Zones as part of broader community economic development activities (e.g., façade improvements, strategic planning, local investment strategies).
  • Additionally, the term Enterprise Zone appears in state community development contexts as a designation that helps communities plan targeted investment and may enhance eligibility for various state assistance programs.

What this means:

The Pennsylvania Enterprise Zone Program (EZP) Tax Credit is an initiative under the Neighborhood Assistance Program (NAP) that provides tax credits to private companies investing in the rehabilitation, expansion, or physical improvement of buildings and land within designated Enterprise Zones.

Key Details

  • Credit Amount: Up to 25% of the amount invested in eligible projects.
  • Cap: Maximum of $500,000 in total tax credits per project.
  • Carry-Forward: Unused credits can be carried forward for up to 5 years or transferred/sold.

Eligibility

To qualify for the credits, your project must meet the following criteria:

  • Location: The investment must fall within a portion of a distressed community officially designated as an Enterprise Zone, Keystone Main Street, or Keystone Communities Enterprise Zone.
  • Job Creation: Employment or retraining opportunities must be created for low-income individuals living within the designated zones. Jobs must be full-time, exceed the state minimum wage, offer a family-sustainable wage, and include benefits.
  • Eligible Activities: Includes building and land improvements, engineering, architecture, and acquisition in addition to rehabilitation.

Former designated Enterprise Zone:

  • Along the 119 corridor through the county

New Enterprise Zone:

  • All major corridors through the county

Additionally, this layer uses a the Mercator projection system, which is used for all online WebGIS maps/layers.

 

Additional Info:

Keystone Innovation Zone (KIZ)

Purpose:
An incentive program designed to encourage innovation and support the growth of young, innovative companies by offering tax credits to for-profit businesses in specific industry sectors.

Key Features:

  • Tax credits (up to a cap, typically $100,000 per company per year) tied to growth in gross revenues generated within the KIZ.
  • Credits can be carried forward and, in some cases, sold or reassigned to other taxpayers.
  • Eligibility generally requires that a business:
    • Is located within a designated KIZ.
    • Has been in operation less than eight years.
    • Operates within targeted industry sectors defined for that zone (e.g., technology, life sciences).

Who it’s for:
Innovative growth companies and startups in sectors the state has targeted for technology and entrepreneurship development.

Goal:
To connect educational and research institutions with private sector businesses and foster high-growth entrepreneurial activity.

The Pennsylvania Enterprise Zone Program (EZP) Tax Credit is an initiative under the Neighborhood Assistance Program (NAP) that provides tax credits to private companies investing in the rehabilitation, expansion, or physical improvement of buildings and land within designated Enterprise Zones.

Key Details

  • Credit Amount: Up to 25% of the amount invested in eligible projects.
  • Cap: Maximum of $500,000 in total tax credits per project.
  • Carry-Forward: Unused credits can be carried forward for up to 5 years or transferred/sold.

Eligibility

To qualify for the credits, your project must meet the following criteria:

  • Location: The investment must fall within a portion of a distressed community officially designated as an Enterprise Zone, Keystone Main Street, or Keystone Communities Enterprise Zone.
  • Job Creation: Employment or retraining opportunities must be created for low-income individuals living within the designated zones. Jobs must be full-time, exceed the state minimum wage, offer a family-sustainable wage, and include benefits.
  • Eligible Activities: Includes building and land improvements, engineering, architecture, and acquisition in addition to rehabilitation.

Former designated Enterprise Zone:

  • Along the 119 corridor through the county

New Enterprise Zone:

  • All major corridors through the county

results.description:
This dataset is designed to represent and identify the property boundaries in Lexington-Fayette County. The original dataset was created in late 1990's by a third party that converted existing paper maps to digital GIS files. The data has since been updated by georeferencing recorded plats for corrections and new additions. In cases where the plats do not appear accurate, aerial photos are utilized in attempt to properly locate the property lines. The only except for this process are changes to highway right-of-way in which calls are run from deeds. The geometry of this data is not of survey quality and should not be used for survey purposes. The data is intended for general reference purposes only.

As part of the basemap data layers, the parcel boundary map layer is an integral part of the Lexington Fayette-Urban County Government Geographic Information System. Basemap data layers are accessed by personnel in most LFUCG divisions for basic applications such as viewing, querying, and map output production. More advanced user applications may focus on thematic mapping, summarization of data by geography, or planning purposes (including defining boundaries, managing assets and facilities, integrating attribute databases with geographic features, spatial analysis, and presentation output).
results.snippet: Representation of the property boundaries in Lexington-Fayette County, Kentucky.
